cases.title: A bulk discount and VAT shown line by line
cases.class: Pricing and tax interaction across files
cases.story: A takes 10% off a line of ten or more, in pricing.ts. B shows the VAT on each line, and in tax.ts works it out from the product's price times the quantity, which is what a line cost on B's base. Together, a discounted line is taxed on its price before the discount.

a.why: ten or more of an item take 10% off

fact.sentence: Ten or more of an item take 10% off the line, before VAT is added

b.why: show the VAT on each line of a quote

fact.sentence: A quote shows the VAT on each line

cases.resolution: tax.ts takes the line's price as charged (lineVat(cents)), and pricing.ts passes it the discounted line.

a.sentence: Ten or more of an item take 10% off the line, before VAT is added

b.sentence: A quote shows the VAT on each line

cases.title: A function's meaning changes under a new caller
cases.class: API producer and caller disagree across files
cases.story: A changes products() in catalog.ts to list only what's in stock, and the callers it knows about (the shop page, the product list) now hide sold-out products, as A meant. B adds a product page in index.ts that looks products up with findProduct(), which goes through products(): on B's base that finds every product. Together, the page for a sold-out product is a 404. The types are unchanged, so the type-checker has nothing to say.

a.why: stop listing products that are sold out

fact.sentence: Sold-out products aren't listed

b.why: give each product an API page

fact.sentence: Each product has an API page that says whether it's in stock

cases.resolution: catalog.ts gains catalogEntry(id), a lookup in the whole catalog, and the product page uses it; products() keeps A's meaning.

b.sentence: Each product has an API page that says whether it's in stock

cases.title: Two limits on the same line, and a repair that keeps one
cases.story: A caps a basket line at 99; B caps it at what's in stock. Both rewrite the same validation line in cart.ts, so Git stops at a text conflict. The seeded repair keeps one side of the conflicting line (git merge -X theirs: B's), which compiles, reads plausibly and passes B's check, and silently drops A's cap. It stands in for a hurried resolution or a repair that picks a side; it is not Canon's repair model, which the deployed run uses.

a.why: a basket line holds at most 99

fact.sentence: A basket line holds at most 99 of a product

b.why: never sell more than is in stock

fact.sentence: The basket can't hold more of a product than is in stock

merge.repaired: seeded lossy repair: git merge -X theirs (B's side of each conflicting hunk)

repair.label: seeded lossy repair: git merge -X theirs (B's side of each conflicting hunk)

cases.resolution: Both limits, one check each: at most 99 per line, and no more than is in stock.

a.sentence: A basket line holds at most 99 of a product

b.sentence: The basket can't hold more of a product than is in stock

cases.title: A stored basket changes shape under a new writer
cases.story: A lets a basket line carry a gift note, so the Cart Durable Object now stores { productId: { qty, note } } instead of { productId: qty }, and reads baskets saved in the old shape too. B adds 'take one back out', written against the old shape: it reads lines[id] as a number and writes it back. Together, taking one egg out deletes the whole line from storage (an object compared with 1 is never greater). Each method names its own storage type, so the type-checker can't see the mismatch.

a.why: let a basket line carry a gift note

fact.sentence: A basket line can carry a gift note

b.why: let a shopper take one back out

fact.sentence: A shopper can take one of a product back out of the basket

cases.resolution: takeOne() reads the basket through A's read() and changes the line's qty, so it works on both stored shapes.

a.sentence: A basket line can carry a gift note

b.sentence: A shopper can take one of a product back out of the basket

cases.title: Prices move from cents to dollars under a new reader
cases.story: A stores catalog prices in dollars (the product API gives dollars) and converts with cents() everywhere it found a price: pricing and the shop page. B adds a price list for the till, written when price meant cents, so it formats p.price as cents. Together, the till says eggs cost $0.04. Both are numbers, so the type-checker can't tell.

a.why: the product API should give prices in dollars

fact.sentence: The product API gives prices in dollars

b.why: print a price list for the till

fact.sentence: The till prints a price list with every product's price

cases.resolution: The till formats cents(p), A's conversion, instead of p.price.

a.sentence: The product API gives prices in dollars

b.sentence: The till prints a price list with every product's price

cases.title: A shared setting changes under a module that relies on its old value
cases.class: Config or default change against a dependent module
cases.story: A raises LOW_STOCK in config.ts from 5 to 10, so the shop page warns shoppers earlier. B adds a restock list in index.ts that names the products at or below LOW_STOCK, which is 5 on B's base and exactly what B's requirement says. Together, the restock list also names a product with 8 left.

a.why: warn shoppers when ten or fewer are left

fact.sentence: The shop page warns when ten or fewer of a product are left

b.why: a restock list for the stock room

fact.sentence: The restock list names the products with five or fewer left

cases.resolution: config.ts gains RESTOCK_AT = 5 for the restock list; LOW_STOCK stays the shop page's warning level.

a.sentence: The shop page warns when ten or fewer of a product are left

b.sentence: The restock list names the products with five or fewer left
